issues.legal_issue: A will made while the testator lacks a sound disposing state of mind is not legally valid, and suspicious circumstances surrounding its preparation must be dispelled by its propounder.
material_facts: The testator was physically weak and suffering from typhoid, and the evidence supported that he was delirious when the will was executed; he died a week later.
The testator was young, below average in intelligence and understanding, and had lived with the beneficiary, who had considerable influence over him and his mother.
The beneficiary took a prominent part in arranging the scribe and attesting witnesses and procuring writing materials.
The will gave the beneficiary most of the property absolutely, while giving the testator’s mother only limited interests.
The evidence offered to show that the testator was of sound mind on the day of execution was not accepted.
issues.conclusion: The will was not executed in a sound and disposing state of mind and was not legally valid or binding on the appellant.
issues.legal_principle: The party propounding a will bears the burden of satisfying the court that it is the will of a free and capable testator. Where circumstances raise a well-grounded suspicion that the will does not express the testator’s mind, the propounder must remove that suspicion and affirmatively establish that the testator knew and approved of the document’s contents. A propounder’s prominent role in preparing or procuring execution of a will that confers substantial benefits on the propounder is itself a suspicious circumstance requiring vigilant and cautious scrutiny. The Court applied Barry v. Butlin, Fulton v. Andrew, Tyrrell v. Painton, and Sarat Kumari Bibi v. Sakhi Chand.

predicates.will_validity_appeal: The validity of a will is challenged in an appeal.
predicates.testator_physically_weak_at_execution: The testator was physically weak when the will was executed.
predicates.evidence_of_delirium_at_execution: Evidence indicated that the testator was delirious when the will was executed.
predicates.beneficiary_propounder_took_prominent_pa: The person propounding the will took a prominent part in arranging or procuring its execution.
predicates.will_conferred_substantial_benefit_on_pr: The will conferred a substantial benefit on the person propounding it.
predicates.propounder_had_influence_over_testator: The person propounding the will had considerable influence over the testator.
predicates.will_is_not_legally_valid: The will is not legally valid.

issues.definition: When a will-validity appeal involves the stated condition of the testator and the propounder’s influential role in procuring a will that substantially benefits that person, the will is not legally valid.

issues.legal_issue: An unresolved material issue that the lower appellate court did not examine must be remitted for a finding before the appeal is finally disposed of.
material_facts: The High Court had not examined whether the Hindu Succession Act applied or who was entitled to succeed to the estate.
The Supreme Court had decided that the will was invalid but could not finally dispose of the appeal without a finding on the unresolved succession issue.
The Supreme Court directed the High Court to hear the parties and make its finding on the evidence already given, without permitting additional evidence.
issues.conclusion: The appeal was remanded to the High Court for a finding on the unresolved succession issue on the existing evidence, after which the appeal would be heard further.
issues.legal_principle: Where a material question arising in an appeal has not been examined by the High Court, the Supreme Court may remit the matter for the High Court to hear the parties and record a finding on the evidence already adduced.

predicates.civil_appeal: The proceeding is a civil appeal.
predicates.material_issue_not_examined_by_high_cour: The High Court has not examined a material issue that must be resolved before the appeal can be finally disposed of.
predicates.matter_is_remitted_for_finding: The matter is remitted for a finding on the unresolved issue.

issues.definition: When a civil appeal contains a material issue that the High Court has not examined, the matter is remitted for a finding.
